title: Derived Hom descent for a normalized native functor
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $X$ a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible in every local ring. Let $D$ be a normalized native functor of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-normalized-functor]. For every two source objects $K,L$, the map $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}(D.JK,D.JL)$ induced by $D.J$ is bijective.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), split from native realization proof steps 3, 6 and 7.

proof.text: Use the finite tensor normalization comparison. Its concrete exact transport H from native modules to condensed modules is an equivalence. Its finite functors F_E are full and faithful, and its object and representative equations express the native image of a common-stage arrow by the usual condensed tensor associators.

For injectivity choose one finite field representing both source arrows. Apply H and the representative equation and cancel the object comparisons and scalar associators. Derived extension E to the algebraic closure is faithful by the split coefficient inclusion. Cancel the finite scalar isomorphisms, then use faithfulness of F_E. The original representatives, hence their quotient classes, are equal. No eventual-injectivity clause is needed.

For surjectivity conjugate H of the given native arrow by the object comparisons. The Hom-surjectivity clause of the existing condensed filtered two-colimit represents it at one common finite field. Conjugate that arrow by the inverse finite scalar comparisons and take its preimage under the full finite functor. The representative equation and the two inverse-isomorphism identities identify its native image with the given arrow, since H is faithful. This proves the original map bijective for every two source objects, in particular for shifts.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), with Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15. Finite tensor normalization followed by explicit injectivity and surjectivity; injectivity uses the proved split-coefficient derived-faithfulness theorem.
